You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Birchwood wayfinding","question":"Can the clerk mark installation complete for the northern signs?","claims":{"A":"The signs were mounted facing the paths on opening day.","B":"The signs were made of wood.","C":"The signs were delivered on Thursday."},"sources":{"S1":"signed carrier slip records Thursday delivery.","S2":"inventory lists four aluminium signs.","S3":"the foreman's work order describes the intended orientation and was checked off without requiring an orientation photograph."},"follow_up":{"S4":"an independent time-stamped opening-day survey shows one of the four signs facing away from the path."}}

message.content: {"claims":{"A":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S4"],"confidence":90},"B":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S2"],"confidence":95},"C":{"status":"supported","citations":["S1"],"confidence":100}},"note":"Claim A is contradicted by S4, which shows a sign facing away from the path on opening day, disproving that all signs were mounted facing the paths. Claim B is contradicted by S2, which lists the signs as aluminium, not wood. Claim C is supported by S1, which records delivery on Thursday. The foreman's work order (S3) does not confirm orientation but indicates intended orientation was checked off without photo evidence. Overall, the clerk should not mark installation complete for the northern signs due to the incorrect orientation evidenced by S4."}

parsed.note: Claim A is contradicted by S4, which shows a sign facing away from the path on opening day, disproving that all signs were mounted facing the paths. Claim B is contradicted by S2, which lists the signs as aluminium, not wood. Claim C is supported by S1, which records delivery on Thursday. The foreman's work order (S3) does not confirm orientation but indicates intended orientation was checked off without photo evidence. Overall, the clerk should not mark installation complete for the northern signs due to the incorrect orientation evidenced by S4.
